prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# 10 Stock Picks as of January 2, 2019

**A caveat first:** I'm writing this in 2026, so I already know how 2019–2024 turned out. I've limited the reasoning to what was knowable in January 2019, but I can't fully set aside what I know. Treat this as an exercise shaped by hindsight, not a fair test of stock-picking skill or a valid backtest.

## Market backdrop (January 2019)
- The S&P 500 just fell almost 20% from its September peak, bottoming on Christmas Eve.
- The Fed raised rates again in December, to 2.25–2.50%.
- The US–China trade war and fears of slowing growth are weighing on markets. Apple cut its revenue guidance after today's close.
- Valuations have come down sharply, especially in high-quality tech.

## The 10 picks

| # | Company | Thesis (as of Jan 2019) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure is growing about 75% a year. The shift to Office 365 subscriptions makes revenue more recurring and lifts margins. |
| 2 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Dominant search franchise, plus YouTube and Cloud. Reasonably valued once its large cash pile is excluded. |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS and the fast-growing ad business should keep expanding margins. |
| 4 | **Visa (V)** | Takes a cut of the global shift from cash to digital payments, with very high margins and little credit risk. |
| 5 | **UnitedHealth (UNH)** | The largest managed-care company, and its Optum health-services arm is growing fast. Defensive earnings growth. |
| 6 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Leads the industry in advanced chipmaking and is ahead of Intel on 7nm. Trades at about 15x earnings. |
| 7 | **Nvidia (NVDA)** | Down about 50% after excess inventory from the crypto-mining bust. Its position in gaming, data-center and AI chips looks intact. *(This is the pick most open to hindsight bias.)* |
| 8 | **Adobe (ADBE)** | Creative Cloud subscriptions are very sticky, and the Marketo and Magento deals expand its business-software reach. |
| 9 | **Costco (COST)** | The membership model holds up in recessions, customers are loyal, and online sales are growing. |
| 10 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | A best-in-class bank with strong capital, rising buybacks and dividends, and some benefit from higher rates. |

## Portfolio notes
- **Concentration:** About 70% of this list is tech or tech-adjacent. The S&P 500 is already heavy in tech, so beating it requires taking larger positions in your highest-conviction names.
- **Sizing:** Consider equal weights (10% each) and rebalance once a year.
- **Key risks:**
  - A recession in 2019–2020.
  - The trade war escalating, which would hit TSM and NVDA hardest.
  - Antitrust action against the big tech companies.
  - Healthcare-policy changes, such as "Medicare for All," hurting UNH.
- **Base rate:** Most professional stock pickers fail to beat the S&P 500 over five-year periods. A low-cost index fund is a strong default, and a concentrated portfolio like this one could easily underperform.

This is an illustrative exercise, not personalized financial advice.

I can also show how these 10 stocks actually performed against the S&P 500 from January 2019 to January 2024.
